checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: optional GameModule.draw_ui(canvas, state) hook -> Engine composition + describe capability -> tests, docs, ADR and gates

impact_assessment.why: An engine-only HUD cannot show game state; games need a supported way to draw health/score/custom panels with the same dependency-free UI toolkit.
impact_assessment.benefits: External games can add HUDs and panels without forking the engine, while the five required GameModule operations stay unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: optional draw_ui hook and describe capability; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the game draws into a per-frame Canvas, never the engine's menu.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Hook/no-hook capture test, describe test, hidden-overlay behavior documented and the full 6/6 gate.

[1/3] Plan: Canvas text/button metadata -> schema-2 UI report + --start-paused -> UI diff, tests, docs, assets, ADR and gates

impact_assessment.why: Human UI pixels are now real, but AI reports cannot see HUD labels, buttons, selection or pause state; UI regressions remain pixel-only.
impact_assessment.benefits: Reports expose structured UI elements for AI/UI analysis, and baseline diffs can name added/removed/changed labels and buttons.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: report schema 1->2 with an optional ui field, new --start-paused flag; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: UI metadata is read-only presentation data.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Backward-compatible comparison of missing ui, schema tests, deterministic headless UI reports and the full 6/6 gate.

[1/3] Plan: TextureData + PNG/checker sources -> cached GL texture sampling and textured sample floor -> schema-3 material reports, tests, docs, ADR and gates

impact_assessment.why: Meshes carry UVs but materials cannot use a texture; a 3D engine and AI graphics reports need textured surfaces and material metadata.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games can load RGBA PNG textures or use a procedural checker; reports name texture dimensions and hashes, and the sample demonstrates the feature.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Material.texture, TextureData API, report schema 2->3; dependency: stdlib PNG reader plus existing PyOpenGL; concurrency: none; state: immutable texture data and a renderer-owned GPU cache.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Texture validation/round-trip tests, textured readback integration test, schema compatibility and the full 6/6 gate.

[1/4] Plan: stable scene-local node IDs, tags/layers/components and typed queries -> schema-4 identity metadata and identity-aware report diff -> docs/ADR -> full gates

impact_assessment.why: The scene keys nodes only by name, so duplicate names cannot be addressed and the engine has no game-agnostic way to attach behaviour or query entities; scene identity is the first core roadmap item.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games get stable per-scene IDs, tags, layers, optional typed components and Scene.query/find helpers; AI reports and baseline diffs can address nodes by identity instead of a colliding name.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Node fields and Scene query API plus report schema 3->4; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none (per-scene counter); state: IDs are assigned on attach/first traversal and preserved across reparenting, reports stay read-only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Tests first for IDs/tags/layers/components/queries, backward-compatible comparison for schema 1-3, determinism across two scenes, full pytest and aikit check.

[1/5] Plan: serializable scene document -> stdlib JSON API -> vanilla web console and WebGL2 viewer -> CLI --serve, docs/ADR -> full gates and browser check

impact_assessment.why: The engine's AI surface is CLI-only and the human surface is a desktop window; AI clients and browser users need the same game contract, scene state and deterministic simulation over a local web API.
impact_assessment.benefits: One JSON contract for CLI, AI clients and a browser console; a WebGL2 preview of any exported scene; CORS-enabled localhost endpoints for describe, scene and simulate; no new runtime dependencies or GPU requirement on the server.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new keystone.web API, scene schema 1 and --serve/--host/--port flags; dependency: Python stdlib plus existing keystone modules, vanilla JS with no CDN; concurrency: threaded HTTP requests share one game session behind a lock; state: localhost-only default, simulation mutates the in-memory game, no files or secrets exposed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure scene-serialization tests, HTTP integration tests on an ephemeral port, static-asset and CLI validation tests, a manual browser/console check, and the full pytest/aikit gate.
